service.name: Private party entertainment in Colorado Springs
service.serviceType: Live music for private parties, wedding weekends and milestone celebrations
service.description: An acoustic duo, solo guitarist or trio for Colorado Springs private parties, wedding weekend dinners and milestone celebrations at resorts, clubs and homes.

faqs.q: Do you book an acoustic duo in Colorado Springs?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the size this city books most. Voice and guitar, or guitar and upright bass, playing covers guests can name at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table. It fits an 8 by 6 foot corner on one dedicated 20-amp circuit, which suits a resort terrace, a club dining space or a house without anything being built for it.

faqs.q: Does travel from Denver add to a Colorado Springs quote?
faqs.a: One flat Front Range line on the quote, covering the run down I-25 and back. There is no mileage arithmetic and no lodging line, because the Springs is a drive home rather than a mountain date, and the fee for the music itself is the same one a Denver host sees.

faqs.q: Can music play outdoors on a Colorado Springs terrace?
faqs.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it and a move-indoors call agreed before the day. Wind comes off the front of the range in the afternoon and the temperature drops fast once the sun is behind it, so the call gets made early and a duo is inside in a few minutes.

faqs.q: What size fits a wedding welcome party or rehearsal dinner here?
faqs.a: A solo player or a duo. Most of a wedding weekend is dinners and drinks rather than dancing, and those evenings want music underneath the conversation. A trio is the booking when the welcome party is genuinely going to turn into a floor, and the wedding cocktail hour itself has its own page.

faqs.q: Does the altitude in Colorado Springs change anything?
faqs.a: Not for the music. The city sits at about 6,035 feet, which guests from sea level notice and players do not. The mountain corridor is a different question, and altitude planning for Vail, Aspen and Breckenridge is set out on our mountain page rather than here.
